---
title: "Suggest an improvement"
---

You may notice a question we have missed, advice that needs correcting, a section that no longer earns its place, or a source that would make the handbook stronger. You do not need to edit the handbook or arrive with finished wording. Tell us what a graduate researcher needs and why it matters.

[Suggest an improvement](https://github.com/hareshsuppiah/handbook-for-the-recently-enrolled/issues/new?template=share-feedback.yml){.btn .btn-primary}

The current form is hosted by GitHub and requires a free GitHub account. GitHub calls a suggestion an “issue”, but you are not reporting a software bug and you will not be asked to change the book yourself. A simpler form without a GitHub login is planned.

Not sure what to write? Read the [short guide with worked examples](how-to-help.qmd).

## Before submitting

Do not include identifiable personal information, participant data, private correspondence, complaints casework, confidential research, unpublished results you cannot share, credentials or security-sensitive details. Describe the general problem and redact specifics.

## Useful feedback includes

- a graduate-research question or situation the handbook does not answer;
- an inaccurate, unclear or potentially misleading passage;
- a section that should be shortened, combined, replaced or removed;
- a missing checklist, template, example or decision aid;
- an authoritative source relevant to a handbook claim;
- a barrier that makes the handbook difficult to read, navigate or access;
- a local rule or practice that needs a clearer boundary.

Submit one feedback record for each distinct problem. Describe the problem without trying to rewrite the page yourself.

## What happens next

1. The feedback is checked for private information, duplicates and existing coverage.
2. The evidence, scope, likely consequence and local-policy boundaries are reviewed.
3. Haresh, as project lead and founding editor, decides whether the suggestion is approved, needs more evidence, is deferred, duplicates existing work or is outside the handbook's scope.
4. Approved improvements are researched, drafted and tested.
5. Haresh reviews the actual change before deciding whether to publish it.

Approval authorises an AI agent or maintainer to prepare a proposed change. It does not publish that change. Haresh reviews the actual wording and evidence before anything is released.

## Credit

You may request named credit, organisational credit, pseudonymous credit or no public credit. Sending feedback does not automatically make someone an author of the handbook.
